questions.question: Accurate use of capitalisation in writing serves which primary purpose?
questions.explanation: Accurate use of capitalisation makes communication easier to understand.

questions.question: The learning objectives of the capitalisation topic include defining which term?
questions.explanation: One objective is to define the term punctuation.

questions.question: Differentiating between hyphen and dash is listed as which type of objective?
questions.explanation: The learning objectives include differentiating between hyphen and dash.

questions.question: Every first letter in a sentence must be written in which case?
questions.explanation: The first letter of every sentence is written in a capital letter.

questions.question: In the sentence "An albino rat is used for experiment", the word "An" is capitalised because it is which element?
questions.explanation: The first letter of a sentence is capitalised.

questions.question: The statement "the material is arranged orderly" violates which capitalisation rule?
questions.explanation: The first word of a sentence should be capitalised.

questions.question: Proper nouns and adjectives used as proper nouns are capitalised in which position?
questions.explanation: Proper nouns are capitalised in any position they occur in the sentence.

questions.question: The major difference between proper nouns and common nouns is based on which feature?
questions.explanation: Capitalisation is the major difference between proper and common nouns.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a proper noun?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is a specific place name and is a proper noun.

questions.question: In the sentence "Mr Michael comes from Urugbam-Erei", the word "Michael" is capitalised because it is which type of noun?
questions.explanation: Michael is a specific person's name, which is a proper noun.

questions.question: The word "English" in "He speaks English fluently" is capitalised because it is which part of speech?
questions.explanation: English is a proper adjective derived from a proper noun.

questions.question: In "He worships in the Catholic Church", the word "Catholic" is capitalised because it is which type of adjective?
questions.explanation: Catholic is a proper adjective referring to a specific religious group.

questions.question: The days of the week are classified as which type of nouns?
questions.explanation: Days of the week are proper nouns and should be capitalised.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct capitalisation for a day of the week?
questions.explanation: Days of the week begin with a capital letter.

questions.question: In the sentence "The man travelled on Saturday last week", the word "Saturday" is capitalised because it is which element?
questions.explanation: Saturday is a day of the week and is a proper noun.

questions.question: The months of the year are examples of which type of nouns?
questions.explanation: Months of the year are proper nouns and should be capitalised.

questions.question: Which of the following months is correctly capitalised?
questions.explanation: Months begin with a capital letter.

questions.question: In the sentence "The month of January is usually difficult", the word "January" is capitalised because it is which element?
questions.explanation: January is a month of the year and is a proper noun.

questions.question: In a poem, the first word of every line is usually capitalised regardless of whether it is which type of word?
questions.explanation: The first words of every line of a poem are capitalised irrespective of whether the word is a proper noun or not.

questions.question: The example "The difference they carry" illustrates which capitalisation rule?
questions.explanation: The first word of a poem line is capitalised.

questions.question: The words "The brains or the brawns" from Emori (1989) demonstrate capitalisation of which element?
questions.explanation: The first word of a poem line is capitalised.

questions.question: Titles of people are written beginning with a capital letter especially when the title does what?
questions.explanation: Titles are capitalised especially when they precede the name of the person referred.

questions.question: Which of the following is correctly capitalised according to the title rule?
questions.explanation: The title "Professor" should begin with a capital letter when preceding a name.

questions.question: In "Governor Ayodele", the word "Governor" is capitalised because it is which element?
questions.explanation: Governor is a title preceding a name and should be capitalised.

questions.question: The first person singular pronoun "I" is written in which case?
questions.explanation: The pronoun I is always written in a capital letter.

questions.question: In the sentence "I will like to eat rice", the word "I" is capitalised because it is which element?
questions.explanation: The first person singular pronoun I is always capitalised.

questions.question: The sentence "Aja and I shall travel soon" demonstrates capitalisation of which word?
questions.explanation: The pronoun I is always capitalised.

questions.question: The first word in a title or subtitle of a book or journal is written in which case?
questions.explanation: The first word in a title or subtitle is capitalised.

questions.question: In the title "Introductory English phonetics and phonology: For second language learners", the word "Introductory" is capitalised because it is which element?
questions.explanation: The first word of a title is capitalised.

questions.question: The word "For" in the subtitle "For second language learners" is capitalised because it is which element?
questions.explanation: The first word of a subtitle is capitalised.

questions.question: The first word in an indented quotation is written in which case?
questions.explanation: The first word in an indented quotation is capitalised.

questions.question: In the quotation "The Vowels are produced without obstruction", the word "The" is capitalised because it is which element?
questions.explanation: The first word of an indented quotation is capitalised.

questions.question: The first word of an indented quotation is capitalised even if the word is originally what?
questions.explanation: The first word is capitalised even if it was originally capitalised in the source.

questions.question: Specific names for departments, subjects and courses should be written with which type of letter?
questions.explanation: Specific names for departments, subjects and courses are capitalised.

questions.question: Which of the following is correctly capitalised according to rule 10?
questions.explanation: Specific names of departments and subjects are capitalised.

questions.question: The course code "ELS 101" should be written in which case?
questions.explanation: Course codes are specific names and should be capitalised.

questions.question: The sentence "my friend and i went to the market" violates which two capitalisation rules?
questions.explanation: The first word "my" and the pronoun "i" both need capitalisation.

questions.question: In the sentence "We visited the university of nigeria, nsukka", which words are incorrectly capitalised?
questions.explanation: University of Nigeria, Nsukka is a proper noun and should be fully capitalised.

questions.question: The sentence "pastor okoafor preached on sunday" has errors in capitalisation of which words?
questions.explanation: Pastor is a title and Sunday is a day of the week; both need capitalisation.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly applies capitalisation rules?
options: I will travel in january to see professor Audu.
i will travel in January to see Professor Audu.
I will travel in January to see Professor Audu.
I will travel in January to see professor Audu.
questions.explanation: Pronoun I, month January, and title Professor are correctly capitalised.

questions.question: In the poem line "walk far from the brawns", the word "walk" should be capitalised because it is which element?
questions.explanation: The first word of a poem line is capitalised.

questions.question: The sentence "he is a ghanian who speaks igbo" requires capitalisation of which words?
questions.explanation: He is first word, Ghanian is a proper adjective, and Igbo is a language name.

questions.question: The sentence "the bible says that god is love" requires capitalisation of which words?
questions.explanation: The is first word, Bible and God are proper nouns.

questions.question: In the sentence "we travelled on monday and tuesday", the words that require capitalisation are which of the following?
questions.explanation: We is first word, Monday and Tuesday are days of the week.

questions.question: The sentence "mr audu is a member of the islamic faith" requires capitalisation of which words?
questions.explanation: Mr is a title, Audu is a name, Islamic is a proper adjective.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct application of the rule for titles?
questions.explanation: The title President should be capitalised when preceding a name.

questions.question: The sentence "i read the book introductory english phonetics" requires capitalisation of which words?
questions.explanation: Pronoun I, and the first words of title and proper adjective English.

questions.question: In the quotation "the vowels are produced without obstruction", the first word "the" should be capitalised because it begins which element?
questions.explanation: The first word of an indented quotation is capitalised.

questions.question: The sentence "the man travelled on saturday last week" requires capitalisation of which words?
questions.explanation: The is first word, Saturday is a day of the week.

questions.question: The rule that every first letter in a sentence is written in a capital letter applies to which type of sentence?
questions.explanation: The rule applies to every first letter in a sentence regardless of sentence type.
